ov: A large, heavily built wild cow of sub-Saharan Africa, the only living species in its genus. Males have a bony plate, the “boss”, between the horns. Herds can number from a few to over a thousand, and its power and size mean it has few natural predators, though calves are vulnerable.

why.dg: Trophy hunters prize it for its aggression and power.
why.et: Widely hunted for bushmeat, and farmed on private land for meat and skins.

len: 2.1–3 m head and body (Cape buffalo, the largest)
df: Mainly grass: 6.5–15 kg a day, about 2.2% of its body weight.

cf.tip: The American bison is often called a buffalo, but it isn’t one of the true buffalo.

fx: Females usually stay with their herd for life.
Herds “vote” on where to go: after resting, adult females stand and point their heads in the direction they want.
notes: Aliases include "water buffalo", an Asian species this page doesn’t cover.
